exclude: Runtime: zero page, stack, system state, generated charset, playfield buffer and character-colour lookup; initial packed bytes below $1500 are overwritten by start
Runtime enemy records initialized by $51F5/$5279 and the active-enemy summary at $1D21
Outside the unpacked gameplay payload: loading-picture/code/music leftovers, generated screen memory, input-recording capacity, chips and runtime RAM vectors
Runtime output: the selected 520-character train layout copied here by $452F and rotated during scrolling
Alignment/workspace after the fixed 1000-cell cast panel and before the initialized enemy records
Runtime count and fifteen-byte metadata queue, written by $3D5D and drained by $3D34
extra: Contiguous gameplay payload written backwards by the unpacker, from its first output at $BD5D through its final byte at $1500

comments.text: Initial character template for the top eleven screen rows: TOP, SCORE, TIME, DIST., ROUND and blank sky cells. copy_background_to_working_screen copies this seed with the generated train rows into the working screen each pass; update_hud overwrites its working copy rather than these header labels.
Thirteen template cells replaced with SCORE/TIME or PRACTICE MODE at the start of a game. The remaining cells in this template span contain the time/distance/round legends and blank sky space.
Continuation of the initial blank-sky and HUD template at $1500. These cells precede the generated train-template output beginning at $16B8.

Runtime destination for the selected 520-cell train layout. draw_train_template copies the chosen roof/interior data here and the scroll routines rotate its thirteen forty-byte rows; this output is excluded from authored-data coverage.

Forty initial ground characters cycling $79-$7E. The scrolling routines shift this visible window and copy a character or pair from an earlier repetition to preserve the six-character pattern; this is not a circular rotation of all forty cells.
Second cell of ground_row_seed. rotate_ground_characters restores the second saved outgoing character here after shifting that row right by two.
Fifth cell of the forty-character ground row. wire_death_sequence reads it as the outgoing value before its one-character left rotation of that row.
Ground offsets 34 and 35, saved before the two-cell right shift. These end the first six repetitions of the six-character ground pattern; the physical forty-cell window continues through $18E7.
Ground offset 35, copied to the first cell by one-cell right shifts. This is the end of a 36-cell repeated cycle; the forty-cell window ends at $18E7 and the separator is $18E8.
Zero byte between the forty-cell ground row and the fixed-size cast panel at $18E9. It is copied into the unused tail of the working screen by the four-page background copy.

Twenty-five rows of forty character codes for the cast reveal. Includes THE CAST, THIS IS YOU! and TRAIN GANG with their pictures. The reveal loops read each full row through their fixed forty-column arithmetic, rather than using a text terminator.

A trailing space followed by forty-six zero bytes between the fixed-size cast panel and the runtime enemy records at $1D00. These bytes lie outside the panel's twenty-five rows and are excluded as alignment/workspace.
Entry from the illustrated loader: jump into the game's initialization at $1E06. The machine is a 64 KB Plus/4 with the ROMs paged out.
Jump-table entry used by the loading title to install the music interrupt at $1EAA after the game has unpacked.

Set the stack and TED to 256-character text, generated glyphs at $0800 and colour/screen memory at $D800/$DC00. Clear 1,000 colour cells and 1,000 working screen cells, build the train tiles, clear the game's zero-page state $19-$80, then enter the attract display and start path.
Silence effects, load train tiles, turn the display on and select stage 1 before drawing the title-side train display.
Clear and rebuild the working screen and train tiles, set attract mode, install the music interrupt and enter the game-start controller at $265B.

If the RAM IRQ vector's low byte is already $0A, return. Otherwise wait for raster low byte $CC with interrupts disabled, initialize the music driver at $9D32, clear TED's IRQ flags, point the RAM vector at $1F0A, select raster compare 3 and enable interrupts.

If the RAM IRQ vector's low byte is $27, return. Otherwise wait through raster $CA-$CC, count down $F5 and $F8, and drain $F0 by subtracting 9 on successive waits. Then select the short handler at $1F27 without changing TED's compare register.

Preserve A/X/Y, call the music update through a self-modifying JSR initially targeting $9D38, alternate the raster comparison by XOR $C8, and alternate the call target's low byte by XOR $0D. The two targets are $9D38 and $9D35; return through the shared register restore and TED acknowledgement.

Low operand byte of the music IRQ's JSR at $1F0F. The IRQ XORs it with $0D after each call, alternating $9D38 output-only and $9D35 sequencing-plus-output while it also alternates raster comparisons 3 and 203.
Acknowledge TED's pending flags with ASL $FF09 and return from the interrupt. The music handler falls through here after restoring A/X/Y.

Convert the current carriage distance to HUD text at $1079, then use stage-specific engine width and the background scroll to write the carriage's two displayed digits into the train character buffer. The tables at $1FE8/$1FEB supply the train's digit characters.
Low operand byte of the carriage-number store at $1FB8, changed by the train selector to the selected design's number position.
High operand byte paired with $1FB9. The following instructions finish the left number digit and return from this stage-one display path.
Low operand byte of the carriage-number store at $1FE4, patched with the same selected design position as the store at $1FB8.
High operand byte paired with $1FE5. The following RTS ends the distance-display path before the digit character sequence begins at $1FE8.
Character sequence for a carriage-number digit, read with a masked four-bit distance index; the right digit table starts three bytes later and overlaps this sequence.

Eleven displayed digit character codes $F9,$F0-$F9, indexed by a masked carriage count when updating the number on the moving train. The following bytes are code at $1FF6, so invalid indices can read beyond the digit sequence.
Shift $02/$03 left three times, add its original low byte to the result and add X with carry to the high byte. Used with X=0 to obtain a nine-byte offset from an eight-bit record index.
Load Y with 6 and shift the 16-bit value in $02/$03 left Y times through the shared loop at $200E.
Set source pointer $06/$07 to the selected train's tile stream; $25C3 rewrites these immediate operands for each train design. Continue into the stream reader at $201E.
Low immediate byte of the selected train tile-stream pointer, rewritten by select_train_design. The companion high byte is at $201B.
High immediate byte of the selected train tile-stream pointer. The following store places it into source_ptr's high byte before load_tile_stream decodes the header.

Decode the header's glyph-RAM offset and record count into bitmap and colour-table destinations. Each record holds eight bitmap rows and one colour byte. When the colour's bit 7 is set, skip both stores and retain the previous glyph and colour; otherwise copy the rows and colour. A zero count means 256 records. X must be zero.
Fill the 16-bit byte count in $04/$05 at destination $06/$07 with Y, advancing the pointer and consuming the count. Uses X as the zero index for indirect stores.
Form $1000 + 40*row + column in $02/$03, taking the initial column in $02 and row in $03. Scratch $12 holds carries while the row is multiplied by forty.
Write space ($20) to all 1,024 bytes at $1000-$13FF with indexed stores. Return with Y wrapped to zero.
Clear the working character screen at $1000-$13FF, then fall into the dirty-screen presenter at $20F5.

Consume the queued actor metadata, then compare each of the four working screen pages with $DC00-$DFFF. For changed cells, copy the character and take its colour from the generated lookup at $1400. LAX absolute,Y loads both A and X from the character code; X returns zero.

Check C for practice activation while in attract mode, M for stopping the music interrupt, and Escape for leaving practice. Then poll joystick/Space and two keyboard rows, mapping the first accepted input through $2242 into command byte $08. Return X=0 and carry clear on accepted input or no input.

Select keyboard row A, wait for its latch to settle, then inspect the returned bits in order. Y selects the first command-table slot for this row. A cleared bit selects its mapped command through $2242.

Select the Space keyboard row and joystick port 1. Fire bit 6 produces command $20; otherwise Space and combinations of direction bits select entries in the command table, including diagonal jumps. Pass the remaining state to the common bit scanner.

Twenty-eight command codes shared by joystick combinations and the two scanned keyboard rows. The nine keypad-like movement commands are ASCII digits 1-9; $20 is the release/start action. Zero entries suppress unsupported keys.
Count a ten-step delay in $09 between selecting a keyboard/joystick row and reading TED's input latch.

If attract mode and the stream-effect flag are clear, set TED voice 1 to value $15F with volume 5 and enable bit 4. Start the two-update duration in $34. Leave the other voice's square/noise selection bits intact.
Mutable pitch/envelope byte for the sound of a released bird; $2F8A resets it and the updater at $228E subtracts six while sounding.

While the train is moving, attract mode is off, and no stream effect owns the sound, decrease $228D by six until below $46. Write half the result to TED voice 2's low frequency and derive a falling volume; otherwise clear voice 2's square-wave enable bit.
Copy bytes from source $06/$07 to working destination $02/$03 until a zero byte, consuming the source terminator and advancing the destination only for written characters. Requires X=0.

Write five decimal digits for the unsigned value in $06/$07 to destination $02/$03, using repeated subtraction of 10000, 1000, 100 and 10, then the remaining units. Zero-fill leading positions; X must be zero.

Repeatedly subtract divisor $04/$05 from $06/$07, counting from character '0'. Restore the first underflowing subtraction and write that decimal digit to destination $02/$03, advancing the destination.

Write the value in $08 as three decimal positions to destination $02/$03, using leading spaces for values below 100 or below 10. Consume $08 down to units through the helper at $23AA and return after writing its final digit.
Repeatedly subtract the divisor in $05 from $08, counting the digit from '0' in $04. Restore the first underflow, write the digit and advance destination $02/$03.
An RTS used by retained effect call sites that still prepare frequency/voice parameters. These calls perform no sound-register write here.

Clear attract mode, poll for the Space/fire start command, and otherwise enter the scrolling cast screen. The cast animation repeatedly rebuilds the working screen and returns to the attract train after its two reveal passes.
Clear the working screen, present that clear, then tail-call the selected train tile-stream loader. X is expected to be zero.
Eight design indices 0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3, selected by (round-1)&7. Each train lasts two rounds and the four-design cycle repeats after eight.
Four low bytes of the train tile-stream pointers selected by select_train_design; paired with $257F.
Four high bytes for the train tile-stream pointers: together with $257B these name $6DD7,$76DA,$7FDD,$88E0.
Four low bytes of the tile-stream pointers loaded when entering the final interior section; paired with $2587 and copied into the immediate operand at $28EB.
High bytes for the final-section tile streams selected with $2583; select_train_design patches the load at $28EE.
Low bytes of the selected train's character-layout source, copied into $4530 by the design selector; paired with $258F.
High bytes of the train character-layout sources selected with $258B and consumed by the train renderer at $452F.
Four widths 6,3,11,5 used by the carriage-number layout and saved to engine_width ($80).
Four low bytes patched into the stores at $1FB8 and $1FE4, selecting where the train's carriage-number characters appear; paired with $259B.
High bytes for the number-destination stores patched by select_train_design, paired with $2597.
Low bytes of the train's interior character-layout source, patched into $453E and paired with $25A3.
High bytes for the interior layout sources selected with $259F; patched into $4542.
Low bytes of the engine view copied by draw_stopping_engine at $2AA8; paired with $25AB and patched into $2AA9.
High bytes for the stopping-engine layout sources selected with $25A7; patched into $2AAD.
Low bytes of the train-specific ladder position patched into $2BE5; paired with $25B3.
High bytes of the ladder positions selected with $25AF; patched into $2BE9.
Four threshold values 3,4,3,3 patched into $2BEF, controlling which ladder columns are drawn during the stop animation.
Four values 6,6,7,6 patched into $2C5F as the ladder column's vertical count.
Four low-byte offsets $79,$79,$A1,$79 patched into the addition at $2C04 to place the ladder's lower decoration.

Map (round-1)&7 through eight design slots into four train designs, then rewrite tile-stream pointers and several train-drawing immediate operands from parallel four-entry tables. Also set the engine width in $80.
Thirteen-character normal HUD heading copied to $1508-$1514 when practice is off: ' SCORE  TIME '.
Thirteen-character replacement HUD heading 'PRACTICE MODE', selected when the practice flag $7E is nonzero.

Choose the short interrupt when leaving attract mode; replace the HUD heading for practice, rebuild the screen, reset the new-game counters and begin stage-one initialization. The mode flag controls whether the same engine runs the scrolling attract display.

Reset roof noise operands, derive carriage count as min((round+4)&255,10), initialize stage/train/actors, and run the ready sequence. The byte addition wraps for rounds 252-255, producing carriage counts 0-3 rather than ten.

Present the working screen, update train/background and actor systems through the following calls, then process the stage-one game state. This is the central loop, whose individual calls supply scrolling, input, collisions, scoring, animation and sound.

Stop effects, place the player near the roof exit, run the approach and descent animations with the other train systems, award the stage bonus, then continue scrolling until carriage_progress reaches carriage_count+1 and the scroll offset is zero. Load the interior tile stream at $91E3 and enter stage two.
Initialize stage-two actors and train graphics, run the interior ready sequence, then enter interior_game_loop when its carry result permits play.

Present the screen and update the interior's actors, scrolling, player movement, collisions, HUD, sound and phases. A death enters $30ED. Attract input can return to the cast. Both $3F and $40 must be set and player_x must equal 2 before the final stop sequence begins.

Award the remaining-time bonus and load the train-design-dependent tile stream whose pointer is patched at $28EB/$28EF. Continue updating the final engine view until carriage_progress equals 2*carriage_count+1 and scroll_offset is 1.
Low byte of the final-section tile-stream pointer, rewritten from train_front_tiles_lo by select_train_design before the $28EA immediate load runs.
High byte of the final-section tile-stream pointer, rewritten from train_front_tiles_hi. The following code loads that stream and runs the final approach and slowdown phases.

Keep drawing the final engine view while progressively delaying its scroll. Every sixteenth pass advance the slowdown stage; rotate the background row and wrap wire_position at $54 as the slower scroll advances. After the delay reaches 10, enter the stopped-train celebration.

Clear effect/ladder state, then animate the ladder and stopped-engine view for up to 90 iterations, allowing Space/fire to shorten the live-play wait. Show the next-round message for up to 160 iterations, increment the round byte and restart the roof stage.

Use the selected train's patched source pointer to copy the visible part of the engine view into rows 10-23 of the working screen. Before the final carriage, copy only scroll_offset columns; at 2*carriage_count+1, copy the full 560-character view.
Low byte of the selected stopping-engine character-layout pointer, changed by select_train_design; the high byte is at $2AAD.
High byte of the stopping-engine character-layout pointer. The subsequent routine clips its copy against carriage progress and horizontal scrolling.
Copy the forty-character train-stopped congratulations into working row 5, or select the thirty-four-character instruction for leaving practice when practice_mode is nonzero.
Forty characters drawn after the final stop: 'CONGRATULATIONS!  THE TRAIN HAS STOPPED!'.
Thirty-four-character alternate celebration text asking the player to press Escape to end practice mode; the stored glyph at the key position is read through the game's alphabet.
Copy thirty characters from $2BC0 into the working screen at $11E5, inviting the player to the next round.
Thirty-character message 'GET READY FOR THE NEXT ROUND!!', read by draw_next_round_message.
Draw ladder columns according to the animation step and train-specific threshold: at most three columns for design 1 and two for the other designs. Select decoration $2C4A at step 5 or $2C51 above 5.
Low byte of the ladder's base working-screen address, patched from train_ladder_dest_lo by select_train_design.
High byte of the ladder's base address, patched from train_ladder_dest_hi; the next code selects which ladder columns and bottom decoration to draw.
Train-dependent threshold for deciding which ladder columns to draw; select_train_design writes this comparison byte.
Low-byte offset added to the ladder base address for its bottom decoration; patched from train_ladder_offset, with carry added to the destination high byte.
Zero-terminated character/skip stream for the ladder's final decoration, consumed at $2C40 through draw_shape_stream; its header uses no separate length byte.
Zero-terminated character/skip stream for the earlier lower decoration, selected while the ladder animation step is greater than five.
Write character $7F down a working-screen column, advancing by 40 bytes per row. The loop count is patched at $2C5F for the selected train design.
Immediate row count for draw_ladder_column, set to 6 or 7 by the train selector. The following loop writes the ladder one screen row at a time.
When phase_4 is zero and the ladder step is below 6, increment $33. Leave it unchanged on other calls.

During live moving-train play on phase_4=0, increment $42. The later comparison reads $53, already required to be zero, so the clamp-to-$0F path is not reached through this entry. This routine performs no sound-register write.

Stop effects, clear the active released bird and death frame, then animate the fallen player while the train slows. Rotate its background row and wrap the one-byte wire position, play the death effect as the player reaches row 22, and count down a long wait. Decrement lives and restart the roof or enter game over.

Clip the player's column and select one of four death character streams from $2EFD,$2F0A,$2F17,$2F24. Odd death frames draw one row lower. Prepare the retained sprite metadata and draw the chosen stream into the working screen.
Mutable four-state death animation index, reset by death controllers and advanced during their animation phases.
Four-frame limit used to wrap death_animation_frame. The four shape streams follow this byte.
First death-frame character/skip stream: twelve bytes of components followed by the zero terminator. Used by the death drawer and flashing life icons.
Second death-frame character/skip stream, selected when death_animation_frame is one; its terminator is at $2F16.
Third death-frame character/skip stream, selected for animation index two; its terminator is at $2F23.
Fourth death-frame character/skip stream, selected for the remaining death-frame index; its terminator is at $2F30.
Preserve $04/$05, prepare twice player_y as a retained sound parameter and call the RTS at $23CE, then restore the scratch word. No TED sound register is touched here.

Clear the released bird, reset death/envelope state and animate a roof death after death_reason=2. Advance the background and wire position in the opposite direction from the normal roof death, vary the delay and lower the player to row 22, then decrement lives and restart or enter game over. This path increments TED's border register during the animation.

Clamp the starting player row, animate an interior death through several timed phases and loop the stream effects at $6DBD/$6DC9. After the final wait, subtract a life and restart stage two at $2852, or enter game over. A death reason of $FF skips the first animation phase.
During live moving-train play and phase_2=0, advance $42 up to $0F. The constructed $90|$42 value is overwritten before a sound call, so this entry changes state but writes no sound registers.

Silence effects. Attract mode returns to the cast; live play draws GAME OVER, enables that banner for the next attract display, and keeps the train/HUD animation running. Space/fire starts a new game; expiration returns to the attract setup.

Silence effects, place the player above the screen and animate entry down to row 8 using the rope drawer and roof-ready banner. Count the rope back to zero, returning carry set when ready. Attract-mode Space/fire returns carry clear so the caller can go to the cast/start path.
Draw character $0A down a column from working position $1015 for the positive signed count in $35. Zero or negative counts draw nothing.
Copy eighteen bytes from $33B4 into $10D4. The final copied byte is the $20 opcode at the next routine's entry, which also serves as a trailing space.
Seventeen stored characters of 'STAGE 1    READY!'; the drawer also copies the following JSR opcode ($20) as a trailing space.

Silence effects, position the player at column 38 facing left and move to column 19 while the interior-ready banner and train systems update. Then wait 28 passes and return the result of comparing the last scratch command with zero. Attract inputs can return early with carry clear.
Copy fourteen bytes of 'STAGE 2 READY!' from $3489 into the working screen at $10D5.
Fourteen stored characters 'STAGE 2 READY!', copied by draw_interior_ready_message.

In live play, save the original remaining time in $33. Repeatedly update the HUD and bonus banner, subtract one unit of time and add one to the 16-bit score until time reaches zero; score display appends a zero, so each unit pays ten displayed points. Attract mode returns immediately.
Copy the zero-terminated bonus legend to $10D0, then write the saved starting time from $33 into both its numeric fields. A trailing zero in the legend scales the displayed result by ten.
Zero-terminated 'BONUS    *10=   0 POINTS' layout. draw_bonus_banner overwrites its two blank numeric fields with the saved time value.
Mutable counter incremented by update_bonus_sound; reaching the limit at $3526 resets it to zero and retriggers the chord.
Six-call period for the bonus chord's counter, compared after each increment in update_bonus_sound.
While train_moving is nonzero, advance the six-call sound counter. At zero, start TED voices 1 and 2 at values $234/$2CD with volume 5; otherwise decrease the current volume until it reaches zero.
Copy eighteen characters from $359D to the working screen at $10D3 for the roof-to-interior transition.
Eighteen characters 'STAGE 1  COMPLETE!', read by draw_roof_complete_message.

Write two identical characters across three successive screen rows starting at $1208. Character $68 and the repeated 39-byte row adjustment create the train-exit step detail used by the roof completion sequence.
An RTS kept at the shared tail of drawing callers that have already written their character streams. It performs no sprite-hardware update.

Convert player_x/player_y to a working-screen address and draw the standing, walking, jumping or ducking character stream. Clip entry animation above the screen, choose leg frames from the walking state and add facing offsets to character codes. The streams at $36A7-$36D5 define these poses.

Two torso rows with character pairs $80/$81 and $90/$91 and row skip 39, terminated at $36AF. One hidden torso row advances this source four bytes; two hidden rows select the separate leg stream at $36B0, and three or more draw nothing.
Standing leg pair $A0/$A1, followed by its zero terminator and a retained zero byte; used below the shared torso.
Walking leg pair $B0/$B1 with zero terminator and retained zero byte. The player drawer selects it when the walk-frame byte is nonzero.
Three rows of character pairs for the ducking pose without the extra facing offset; draw_player selects this stream when ducking with zero facing offset.
Alternate ducking stream, beginning with a positive skip command and using character pairs $86/$87,$96/$97,$A6/$A7; selected when facing offset is nonzero.

Dispatch active jump and fall states first. Otherwise set the standing row for the stage, read commands from the recorded attract buffer or real controls, record live non-practice input into that buffer, and dispatch digit commands 1-9 as duck, walk or jump. Space/fire releases a captured bird. Roof walking scrolls the world; free interior movement changes player_x.
While moving horizontally without jumping or falling, toggle the player's walking glyph offset by $10. Otherwise select offset $10 as the resting leg frame.

In stage two, test two ceiling character positions for $26 and allow a jump to latch onto that ceiling. Otherwise add the next signed byte of the selected jump stream to player_y, advance the stream pointer and clear the jumping flag when the following byte is the $88 sentinel. Horizontal motion follows player_direction through the normal walk paths.
Fourteen signed vertical deltas followed by $88, advancing a roof jump from its standing row and returning to it. advance_jump checks the next byte for the sentinel after consuming the current delta.
Twenty-one signed vertical deltas followed by $88 for the longer interior jump; the shared reader may stop it early when ceiling cells permit hanging.

Clear duck/walk state and, when a bird is carried at roof row 8 and its previous release is clear, consume the carried bird and initialize the released bird's position and movement bytes. If the player was ducking, tail-call the common stand-up path.

While its flag, live mode and moving-train flag permit, update the retained jump-envelope bytes $26-$28 and call the no-op sound stub with their parameters. Bounce the pitch increment at its unsigned bounds, decrement the envelope on phase_2=0 and clear the active flag after $28 becomes $FF. It writes no TED sound register.

If the released bird is active and its column is below 39, draw the stream at $3A52 at its $5D/$5E position. Select a glyph offset twice the bird animation frame, reducing frame values above two to one.
Four component glyphs $CA/$CB/$DA/$DB with relative destination skips and a zero terminator. The release and incoming-bird drawers reuse this stream with different glyph offsets.

In flight state 1, inspect the roof's character at the bird's wrapped column; a space starts its falling state. Advance animation and move right on phase_6=0 until its lifetime reaches zero. In the falling state, move down until row 23 and clear the bird and incoming-bird delay.

During live moving-train play, prepare retained sound parameters from $64, call the no-op sound stub, subtract 30 from the envelope and clear its active flag on underflow. No actual sound-register write occurs through this path.
Draw the active incoming bird at row 6 when its column is below 39. Reuse shape_bird with a $20 base glyph offset plus twice the animation frame, reducing frame values above two to one.

Animate the active bird and move it right with a phase gate selected by player_direction: period 2 for left, 3 for still and 4 for right. Clear it at column 80. While inactive, count its delay down by two and spawn at column zero when that countdown is nonnegative and no released bird is active.

Outside engine_room, walk the eight-byte enemy records at $1D00 to their $FF state terminator. Draw each active knife at its recorded position, then visible actor glyph pairs for the current pose and reveal height. Pose 8 uses a separate death stream. Queue retained sprite metadata and add the throw-frame projectile detail for state 3.

Subtract three from the queued-byte count until its signed result is negative, reading each triple through $3D46. The reader restores metadata to scratch variables; this queue-drain path performs no working-screen or TED-screen writes.
Read the triple at $3D87 plus the queue offset: restore its two-byte screen position to $02/$03 and its sprite/glyph selector to $15. Return without drawing.
Take the current actor's column and row from record offsets 2/3 and map pose offset 4 through $3D96. Append that selector and position as a three-byte tuple to $3D87, advancing the count at $3D86.
Mutable byte offset into the retained actor metadata queue. Each queued entry is three bytes; consume_actor_metadata removes them in reverse order.
Fifteen runtime bytes reserved for triples of selector, column and row. queue_actor_metadata appends them; consume_actor_metadata reads and removes them without drawing.
Nine selector bytes indexed by the enemy's pose field when queuing retained sprite metadata: $0A,$1A,$2A,$1A,$0B,$1B,$0C,$1C,$0C.

Eight consecutive six-byte poses for a two-column, three-row enemy. draw_enemy_records uses pose*6, then copies the number of rows its state exposes. The row pairs are raw character codes in the generated train/interior glyph sets.
Alternate zero-terminated character/skip stream for enemy pose 8, with glyphs $AC/$AD/$AE and $BC/$BD/$BE arranged as two three-character rows.

Outside engine_room, first detect an enemy in emergence state 1 using $1D21. Then walk the eight-byte records: move knives on every call, and on phase_3=0 dispatch states 0-4 to waiting/spawn, emergence, walking, throwing or falling handlers. End at the $FF state sentinel.

If the player is alive, decrement this inactive record's delay. Defer spawning when another enemy is emerging; on the roof, scan the train row for a gap and choose an entrance at or beyond column 21. Interior spawns enter walking state at column zero with a round-dependent delay.
Set state 2, derive the walking/throw delay as 18-2*min(round,5), and start the enemy at column 0, row 17, pose 1. Patch the subtraction operand at $3EF9 before storing the delay.
Mutable operand containing twice min(round,5), written just before the spawn-delay subtraction. The remaining state-machine handlers continue after this initialization.

Expose the emerging roof enemy and lift it toward row 7. Switch to walking state 2 at row 8, shift left two columns and select delay 16 in round 1 or 8 later. Reset at column >=80 or outside stage 1; off-screen columns 39-79 can remain in emergence.

State 2: on the roof, approach from columns at least 19 while cycling four walk poses and count down to a throw; in the interior, move right while doing the same. The roof path can move an extra column near the screen edge. Expired delays enter state 3 with pose 5.

State 3: advance the throw counter. At count 4, select pose 4 and start a knife one column left at roof row 8, or two columns right at interior row 17. At count 8, return to walking with delay 32. Large counter values reset the record.

State 4: roof enemies move diagonally down/right, toggle a fall pose and become inactive on reaching row 23, with a delay of 20. Interior enemies count down their state timer and reset when it reaches zero.
Clear the current enemy's state and store eight times min(stage_number,3) as its inactive delay, then continue to the next eight-byte record.

From round 2 onward, draw a two-by-two moving obstacle at row 14, wrapping its horizontal coordinate to 0-39. Its four base characters at $4154 are adjusted by animation and direction before being written.
Preserve the row/column pair, normalize the column modulo 40, compute the screen address and write the source glyph plus the mutable offset at $414A. Restore the caller's row/column before returning.
Immediate glyph offset rewritten to ceiling_obstacle_frame+ceiling_obstacle_direction before the four cells are drawn. The following store and stack restores complete the cell-drawing helper.
Four glyphs $CC,$CD,$DC,$DD forming the moving interior obstacle's two-by-two base pose. draw_ceiling_obstacle adds its animation/direction offset to each.

From round 2 onward, toggle its frame on phase_3=0 and, while the player is alive, add the next signed path delta to its column. Rounds 2-3 gate movement on phase_3 and rounds 4-5 on phase_2; rounds 6 and above advance each call. At the $88 path sentinel, reverse the sign and direction glyph offset and restart the path.
Eighty-three signed horizontal deltas followed by $88. update_ceiling_obstacle consumes a delta, checks the next byte for the sentinel and reverses direction on each restart.

When engine_room is set, draw the character/skip stream at $42D2 at $6F/$70. In live moving-train play, consume its sound-envelope byte through retained no-op sound calls and decrement that envelope when nonzero.
Nine-byte character/skip stream using $CA/$CB/$DA/$DB, with the same byte pattern as shape_bird. The interior replacement glyph set gives these character codes their engine-room appearance.

In engine_room, move the obstacle horizontally and vertically on phase_3=0 in rounds below 3, or phase_2=0 thereafter. Reverse horizontal direction at columns 3 and 37, and vertical direction at rows 12 and 18, triggering the short TED sound at each bounce. Count down that voice-1 sound after motion.
When engine_room is set and brake_triggered is still zero, draw the four-glyph stream at $438D at working position column 27, row 18.
Four-glyph two-by-two detail $EB/$AF/$FB/$BF with row skips and a zero terminator; drawn in the engine section until brake_triggered becomes nonzero.

Rotate thirteen forty-byte train-template rows right by one, shift active enemies and knives right, and update the released bird and ceiling obstacle columns. Increment scroll_offset; at 40 wrap it to zero and advance carriage_progress, adjusting the obstacle coordinate by -40. Refresh the displayed carriage number.

Unless progress and offset are both zero, rotate the thirteen train rows left, move active enemies, knives and other scroll-relative objects left, then decrement scroll_offset. At underflow, borrow one carriage and set offset 39, or clamp at zero progress. Refresh the carriage number.

Outside attract mode, advance a pointer through the signed-terminated rhythm at $4516. For nonzero pattern entries while progress is nonzero and the train moves, enable TED voice-2 noise with a mutable pitch and volume 4, preserving voice 1's enable. Otherwise turn off voice 2's square/noise selection bits.
Low pitch byte used for train noise, reset to $FD at roof-stage initialization and decreased by three per normal roof-death animation pass.
High pitch byte used for train noise, reset to 2 and decremented with borrow during the roof-death slowdown.

Twenty-four rhythm bytes followed by a negative terminator. update_train_noise advances its pointer before reading, restarts it at $4516 on a negative byte, and sounds only for nonzero entries while the train is moving.

Select the current design's roof or interior layout from patched immediate pointers, copy its 520 character cells into template rows at $16B8-$18BF, and refresh the carriage-number characters. Stage 1 selects the roof view; other stages select the interior view.
Low byte of the roof character-layout pointer, written by select_train_design from train_body_screen_lo.
High byte of the roof layout pointer; the following stage test chooses the interior pointer when stage_number is not one.
Low byte of the interior layout pointer, written from train_interior_screen_lo by select_train_design.
High byte of the interior layout pointer; the following copy reads exactly 520 characters into the train template.

Read two forty-character windows from the wire rows at $4604/$4681 using wire_position. Overlay non-space wires, extend support characters into empty cells, and draw the vertical support when the lower row contains character $08.
One hundred twenty-five characters for the upper wire row: an eighty-five-position cycle with forty extra cells for a window that wraps. draw_overhead_wires indexes it with wire_position and Y=39..0.

One hundred twenty-five characters for the lower wire row. The drawer preserves nonempty screen cells for most characters and uses $08 to locate a vertical support; the extra forty cells allow an eighty-five-position scrolling cycle.
Subtract two from the one-byte wire_position. If the signed result is negative, wrap it to $54; no high pointer byte participates in the wire position.

When a pole is active and its column is visible, overlay a vertical pole from row 7 downward while respecting characters at least $09, then draw its horizontal arm. Near its countdown or arm crossing, flash the caution graphic and text on roof live play when the player has no death state.
For an active pole, compute its second support column from pole_x+(pole_x>>2)-5 and, when that is below 40, draw character $09 down eighteen rows from row 7.
Character/skip stream for the roof caution icon. The drawer adds $80 to its high-bit glyph codes before drawing, then continues into the text immediately after its terminator.
Zero-terminated 'CAUTION!' text appended to the caution graphic by draw_pole_and_warning.

While no pole is active, decrement its 16-bit countdown and spawn a pole at column 1 on reaching zero. Active poles move two columns per call; on reaching 40, clear the pole and read the next word from $6D4F. A zero low byte restarts the schedule at its beginning.
Copy all four template pages $1500-$18FF into $1000-$13FF. At carriage_progress=0, erase the off-train columns across twelve rows and draw the ground edge in character $67.
When carriage_progress is nonzero, draw four seven-cell vertical columns across the current scroll boundary, using the sequence $0B,$68,$68,$0B from screen row 13.

Normalize a possibly wrapped horizontal coordinate to 0-39, convert it and row $03 to a working-screen address, and write seven rows of character A. Preserve the caller's row/column word on the stack.

Save ground offsets 34/35 at $18E2/$18E3, shift offsets 0-37 right two cells and restore the saved pair at offsets 0/1. This preserves the six-character repeated ground pattern in a forty-cell window, rather than rotating its final two cells.
On phase_12=0, decrement a nonzero time value unless practice_mode is enabled. Other phase calls and zero time leave it unchanged.

Preserve an existing death; time zero sets reason $FF. At row 8, working-screen cells $11CB/$11CC both containing space mean a gap. Above the roof, an active pole at columns 19-20 is lethal. Continuing paths check enemies, knives and birds. Practice flashes spare lives for ordinary damage.

Scan eight-byte enemy records. Contact at row 6 defeats an active enemy for 30 internal score units; other contact kills, or flashes lives in practice. A released bird can defeat an enemy for 10 units. Attract mode suppresses awards. A defeat or damaging contact returns immediately; only continuing paths check knives and later records.

A released bird crossing the player's horizontal window can cause reason 5 and starts falling. An incoming bird crossing the same window at player row 6 is captured only when none is already carried; clear the incoming bird and start the catch effect at $6D63.

Time zero sets reason $FF. Check the rear-of-train fall position, then enter the engine section at carriage_progress=2*carriage_count-1 and scroll_offset=22. Outside that section, check enemy and knife collisions. Later rounds also check the ceiling obstacle; in the engine section check brake activation and the bouncing obstacle.

From round 2 onward, when player_y<16, normalize the overhead obstacle column modulo 40 and compare it with the player's column. A three-column overlap causes reason 5, or flashes spare lives in practice. Continue to engine-section checks.

In the engine section, a player above row 15 at columns 18-20 sets brake_triggered and starts the effect at $6D79. Compare the bouncing obstacle against a three-column by four-row window around the player; a hit sets reason 6 or flashes the practice indicator.

Track rounded carriage progress, update the high score outside practice, write five decimal digits plus a trailing zero for each score, then write time, remaining distance, round and spare-life figures. Mutable comparison limit set by update_hud to 2*carriage_count+1. The code after the comparison writes distance zero past that limit, spaces for progress zero, or the remaining carriage count, then draws the round and spare lives.

Jump to music_initialize, the shared initializer for two TED, three SID and three DigiMuz logical channels.
Jump to the eight-channel phrase sequencer. Its loop falls into the sound-output routine after updating every channel; the game alternates this entry with music_output_entry in its raster interrupt.
Jump directly to music_output, updating the chip registers and note-age envelopes without advancing the phrase sequencer's duration counters.
Eighty-four low bytes of TED note values, paired with $9D8F. Index $53 is the rest value $03FE; the low range also contains repeated $FE entries. TED instrument handlers use these indices directly.
Eighty-four high bytes paired with music_ted_pitch_lo to form the ten-bit TED note values, including the $03FE rest entry.
Eighty-four low frequency bytes for the optional SID's notes, paired with $9E37. The SID handlers use note index $53 as a separate rest test.
Eighty-four SID frequency high bytes, paired with music_sid_pitch_lo and indexed by the same stored note byte as TED.

Twenty-one rows of nine TED volume values. music_output indexes this grid with fade offset $F0 plus the current envelope value; initialization selects offset 180 and the music-stop path reduces it by nine per step.

Initialize eight order pointers, odd duration counters and even note durations using the initial-order table. Set the TED fade offset to 180, SID/DigiMuz master volumes to 15, clear SID controls/envelopes and pulse widths, and silence the DigiMuz channels. It writes optional-device addresses unconditionally; absent hardware ignores those stores.
Load the current logical channel's loop-order pointer from $A6D7/$A6D8 and continue through the common order reader. A zero high byte in an order word triggers this restart.
Store A/Y as the channel's order-list pointer at $90+X/$91+X, then fall into music_next_phrase. X is the even logical-channel offset 0,2,...14.

Patch two indirect-load operands to the zero-page order pointer at $90+X. Read its next phrase address into $A0+X/$A1+X, restart the order when the word's high byte is zero, and advance the order pointer by two.
Self-modified zero-page operand used to read an order word's high byte. music_next_phrase writes $90+X here before its indirect indexed load.
Self-modified zero-page operand used to read the order word's low byte through $90+X. The remaining code advances that order pointer by two with carry.

For eight logical channels, increment the odd duration counter and decode a new note when it equals the even duration value. $FF advances the phrase order, $FE supplies shared SID ADSR bytes, $F0-$FD selects an instrument, $E0-$E2 selects a TED volume envelope, and $60+N sets duration N. Store the note and advanced phrase pointer, then enter music_output.
Even channel offset saved into this LDX immediate while an envelope command temporarily uses X as an envelope index. The next code reads duration/note bytes and advances the channel's phrase pointer.

Advance the selected volume-envelope index, dispatch instruments for two TED, three SID and three DigiMuz channels, and write each chip's frequency/control/volume registers. Increment the eight note-age counters and set TED's sound mix/volume unless both TED frequencies are the $FE rest value. The IRQ calls this entry both alone and after sequencing.
Immediate OR operand rewritten from the instrument's returned high pitch byte before storing TED voice 1's high bits. Subsequent code emits voice 2 and the optional SID/DigiMuz channels.

Increment $C0,$C2,...$CE after outputting all eight channels. If at least one TED low pitch byte differs from $FE, compute the volume-grid index from the current envelope plus fade offset and write TED's voice selection and volume bits.

Fourteen interleaved code addresses indexed by twice the instrument nibble in $D1+X. Entries 0,6,7 share the plain TED-pitch handler; 8 and 9 share the SID handler. Other entries provide percussion, vibrato and DigiMuz envelope/noise modes.
High-byte alias of the first instrument pointer, read with the same doubled instrument index as music_instrument_dispatch; the table's complete interleaved layout starts at $A20C.

Double the channel's instrument selector in $D1+X, copy its address-table word into the JMP operand at $A239/$A23A, and jump to the selected handler. Handlers return chip pitch in A/Y and may return volume or noise flags in X.
Low byte of dispatch_music_instrument's self-modified JMP target, filled from the fourteen-entry table at $A20C.
High byte of the dynamic instrument target, filled from $A20D. The target handles this channel's pitch/envelope and returns to the caller of dispatch_music_instrument.
For note ages below two, select an initial fixed pitch from $A2ED and choose TED voice-2 noise. Later ages select the rest note $53 through the plain TED-pitch lookup.
Read this channel's note byte at $E0+X and return its TED pitch from the split low/high tables at $9D3B/$9D8F. Instruments 0,6 and 7 dispatch here.

Return rest unchanged. Otherwise mask the note age to sixteen steps, select a signed-magnitude pitch adjustment from $A329, and add or subtract it from the note's TED pitch through the shared adjustment paths.
Return rest unchanged; for other notes, use note-age modulo 16 to select the larger signed-magnitude pitch adjustment at $A319, then adjust the TED pitch with carry or borrow.
Positive pitch increment written by the vibrato handler from its selected adjustment byte. Carry increments the returned pitch high byte.
Magnitude of a negative pitch adjustment, written after masking away bit 7 of the selected vibrato value. Borrow decrements the returned high byte.
Select TED voice-2 noise and return high pitch 3 with a low byte from $A2E1 indexed by the unmasked note age. This entry is not one of the fourteen direct dispatch-table targets.
Add the note-age-indexed byte at $A2D9 to this channel's base TED pitch, propagate carry into its high byte, and select voice-2 noise through $F4. The age index is not masked here.
Return separate low/high pitch bytes from $A2F5/$A2FB, indexed by the unmasked note age. Its normal short events keep the index within the intended percussion contour.
Standalone RTS following the percussion handler; no chip state is changed by entering it.

Eight descending low-byte additions for instrument_ted_noise_sweep, indexed by note age without a mask. Adjacent contours follow immediately, so the score's event duration determines its effective read extent.
Twelve low-pitch values for the retained noise handler at $A2A7, followed by the fixed attack pitches. That handler returns high pitch byte 3.
Four little-endian TED pitch words. instrument_ted_attack selects the first two at ages zero and one; the remaining two words are neighboring retained contour data.
High-byte alias of the first word in music_attack_pitches. The attack handler reads it with twice the note age while the age is below two.
Six low pitch bytes for the age-indexed percussion handler, paired with six high bytes at $A2FB.
Six high pitch bytes paired with music_percussion_low. Adjacent amplitude/contour bytes follow; the reader applies no independent age bound.

Twenty-four bytes of decreasing/amplitude-like constants between the active percussion tables and vibrato tables. The traced direct readers index neighboring contours by unmasked note age; a separate consumer for this retained sequence is open.
Sixteen signed-magnitude pitch adjustments 0,3,5,6,7,6,5,3,0,$83,$85,$86,$87,$86,$85,$83. Bit 7 selects subtraction in the shared vibrato code.
Sixteen signed-magnitude pitch adjustments with maximum magnitude four, selected by note-age modulo 16 for instrument_ted_vibrato_small.
Eighty consecutive bytes forming a rise from $10 to $37 and a matching fall back to $10. No direct address operand in the traced music driver names this ramp; its intended separate use is open.
Return optional SID frequency bytes from $9DE3/$9E37 for an active note, or A=Y=$FF for rest note $53. Instruments 8 and 9 share this entry.
For an active note, return X=$8B as DigiMuz noise-mode/volume flags while A retains the note byte used as the noise period. Rest returns A=X=Y=0 through $A3A5.

For an active note, choose a volume contour according to note duration 6,12 or 24 (otherwise volume 11), then apply a sixteen-phase positive/negative pitch adjustment to the generated DigiMuz period tables at $FC00/$FC60. Return the volume in X and period in A/Y; rest returns zeros.
Twelve output-age volume values selected when the note duration is six sequencer ticks. Output occurs on both alternating music IRQ entries.
Twenty-four volume values selected for a twelve-tick note by instrument_digimuz_vibrato.
